title: Locally routed acquire, elevate, and transfer streams
coverage_gap: Only five correlated LL/HH demonstrations cover acquisition, lift and transfer but no crossed factor cells or failed grasps. A single unrestricted conditioning stream can use target y as a proxy for the stick location or demonstration phase.
reusable_regularity: Use three learned encoders with different receptive fields, routed by a learned soft stage estimator that sees only causal hand/stick relations, heights, aperture and motion. The acquisition encoder cannot see the goal. The elevation encoder adds the pushed-object relation. Only the transfer encoder adds goal edges. A weak training-only action-regime classifier encourages the causal router to distinguish descending acquisition, upward lift, and +x transfer. All actions remain generated by one common conditional U-Net, not by expert action rules.
dependencies_preserved: The router and acquisition encoder do not see goal or absolute x/y, but they retain absolute hand/stick heights, their orientations and local temporal motion. This restricts a shortcut without claiming the whole task is translation invariant.

Every stream has routing weight at least .05. The U-Net also receives a nonzero .25-gain deterministic 39D world-pose skip including all current/previous hand, stick, object2, gripper, orientations and goal. Workspace/table dependencies and required world geometry are never removed by the router.

The pushed object is the declared object2 site-offset point, not an assumed body COM or hidden contact point. Fixed-object and fixed-native-end-effector dependencies remain encoded in world poses and heights.
Two whole observations are processed; native previous slots provide motion. Quaternion sign canonicalization identifies only equivalent physical rotations, and absent zero quaternions remain zero.

evidence_refs.detail: D5-only evidence; no historical candidates or performance.
Confounded factor coverage, observation point conventions, native world action semantics.
Three LL and two HH, all with open-to-closed gripper and large x/z command variation.

Read actions 0:20 (open approach then close/descent), 25:45 (z changes from descent to positive lift), 45:60 (x=1 transfer). Read obs 23:29 and 48:52 showing aperture closure and elevated carried stick. These motivate three weak command-regime labels, not hidden stages.
Read obs 24:27 showing a similar low hand and closing aperture at a different stick x/y and goal y.
Lifted tool and aligned hand posture.
HH low-grasp posture resembles LL local interaction.
Learned module registration and separation of causal conditioning from training targets.
Chunk-start mask, loss hooks, and separately normalized nonnegative auxiliary supervision.

expected_failure_signature: A failed grasp may look locally similar to a completed lift; the router may then over-weight transfer while the tool is not secured. This predicts premature horizontal motion rather than a target-y-dependent initial grasp offset.

Action-regime labels are imperfect stage labels: elevation can end before transfer begins, and transition observations may be ambiguous with a two-observation history. Soft gating should soften but cannot eliminate these mistakes.

The unrestricted world skip can still relearn support correlations, while an overly restrictive local router may miss obstacle or target-dependent stage timing. If routing is ineffective its phase probabilities will not separate the demonstrated motion regimes. No such behavior has been measured here.

required_runtime_fields.raw_history: [B,2,39] all declared fields. Router uses current/previous hand_xyz, object_xyz, gripper, stick quaternion and current absolute z only. Other branches/skip also use object2 poses and goal.
required_runtime_fields.support_fit_state: Mean D5 initial object2_xyz as fixed world origin, JSON-restored
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity encode/decode, native world xyz units .01m and unchanged scalar gripper; only host clips [-1,1]. Fixed 16-step prediction, four-step execution.

training_only_targets.name: stage_label
training_only_targets.source: For each valid D5 chunk start t, actions[t]: transfer if world_dx>.8; otherwise elevate if gripper>0 and world_dz>.02; otherwise acquire. Thresholds annotate demonstrated commands, never generate deployment actions.
training_only_targets.loss: 0.05 times cross entropy against causal router probabilities at the newest observation. Weighted by mask[:,0], divided by mask[:,0].sum(), floor 1. No horizon-padding target contributes. Action epsilon weight 1 and denominator mask.sum()*4 unchanged.
training_only_targets.inference: Labels and actions[t] are unavailable and unused. Router probabilities are predicted exclusively from causal local state, once per condition call.

change_summary: Initial A2: a new three-stream learned causal encoder and weak phase supervision with a complete metric world skip, 114D condition. This differs structurally from A1's fixed edge map. All decisions preceded performance feedback.
